method: Direct inspection of six timestamp-matched reference/commanded/measured RGB thumbnails; unblinded qualitative assessment, not full-video review.
observations: The playground tower, green slide, stairs, planter, trees and surrounding buildings remain recognizable in both arms at the sampled timestamps.
Both generated arms show a pronounced contrast/brightness change between frames 84 and 85.
Later views differ from the reference in staircase scale/placement and foliage/object detail. Both arms retain the overall playground scene; this does not establish geometric or pixel fidelity.

Measured memory lowers mean position error from 0.010054 to 0.008280 reference units (17.64%), but raises endpoint position from 0.018663 to 0.018899 and mean rotation from 0.5736 to 0.7399 degrees; endpoint rotation rises from 1.2631 to 1.9732 degrees.
No near-total scene loss or large invented foreground structure is visible in these six samples. Physical camera reversal and between-sample failures remain untested.
classification: Lower mean position with worse endpoint position and rotation; recognizable playground with appearance/layout drift.
temporal_limitation: Six static timestamps do not establish full-video quality, smoothness, physical motion direction, or absence of between-sample failures.
